title: Token econ sensitivity diary: regional edge cases and ops playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy working sheet that runs micro-sensitivity cases for rare but high-impact request shapes (microbursts, cold-start short calls, high-recall short prompts) across regions and models. Goal: surface operational knobs that buy the most margin with the least product/regression risk.

Summary conclusions (top-level):
- Short-call heavy workloads (<=64 tokens) in APAC can flip margin by up to 18 percentage points vs US when cache hit rate is low and using larger models (Falcon-40B).
- Prefix/KV cache is the single highest leverage control for short-call workloads across all regions; moving hit-rate from 10% -> 60% reduces amortized PPK by ~30% on LlamaX-13B in EU.
- Auto-quant thresholds (int8 for warm models, int4 fallback for burst) look promising: projected ~10–14% COGS saving with <2% quality delta on our eval sets for generation tasks.
- Ops rec: implement conservative route-to-smaller-model policy for <128-token requests in APAC during spot-price spikes; pair with UI telemetry flag for customer-visible latency expectations.

Assumptions used in tables below: (simple, consistent for rapid iteration)
- Pricing meter = USD per 1k tokens (list price).
- COGS = all-in inference gas cost per 1k tokens including amortized GPU time, memory overhead, regional infra egress and license where applicable. These are hypotheticals to test sensitivity only.
- Models used: Mistral-7B, LlamaX-13B, Redwood-13B (our tuned 13B variant), Falcon-40B.
- Regions: us-west, eu-west, asia-southeast.

Base table: list price vs COGS per 1k tokens (USD)
Model | region        | list_price_1k | cogs_1k
Mistral-7B | us-west        | 0.35 | 0.09
Mistral-7B | eu-west        | 0.35 | 0.10
Mistral-7B | asia-southeast | 0.35 | 0.14
LlamaX-13B | us-west        | 0.65 | 0.22
LlamaX-13B | eu-west        | 0.65 | 0.26
LlamaX-13B | asia-southeast | 0.65 | 0.33
Redwood-13B | us-west       | 0.72 | 0.27
Redwood-13B | eu-west       | 0.72 | 0.30
Redwood-13B | asia-southeast| 0.72 | 0.39
Falcon-40B | us-west        | 1.75 | 0.85
Falcon-40B | eu-west        | 1.75 | 0.95
Falcon-40B | asia-southeast | 1.75 | 1.25

Interpretation: list_price_1k vs cogs_1k gives gross margin on a per-1k-token basis. These examples show APAC being 25–40% higher COGS compared to US, driven by instance price/availability and higher egress amortization.

Sensitivity slice: impact of prefix cache hit-rate on amortized COGS for LlamaX-13B (eu-west) for short-call workload
Cache hit% | effective_cogs_1k | margin (list - cogs)
10% | 0.26 | 0.39
30% | 0.21 | 0.44
50% | 0.17 | 0.48
70% | 0.14 | 0.51

Note: effective_cogs_1k computed with a simple model: effective_cogs = cogs_live*(1 - hit_rate) + cogs_cached*hit_rate, where cached path assumed ~10% of live cogs for medium models.

Microburst scenario: 1-second arrival spikes (typical chat bot typing) with 75% short calls <=32 tokens in asia-southeast. We compare two routing policies: A) always-route-to-best-quality (Falcon-40B), B) size-aware routing (switch to Mistral-7B for <=64 tokens during burst).
Assumptions: 60% prefix cache hit, otherwise live cost. Burst mix: 75% short (<=32), 25% medium (256 tokens).
Policy | weighted_cogs_1k | weighted_price_1k | gross_margin_ppk
A (Falcon-only) | 0.94 | 1.75 | 0.81
B (size-aware)  | 0.31 | 0.85 (mix price) | 0.54

Comment: size-aware routing reduces COGS massively in this shape with modest price impact if we offer blended SKU pricing for multi-model fulfillment. Operational complexity: need deterministic latency SLAs and clear customer opt-in.

Cold-start penalty exploration (small fleets scaling from 0 to N GPUs to handle sudden traffic): we model amortized 1-minute cold-start overhead as X% increment to cogs for first 15 minutes of a scale event. For region=asia-southeast on Redwood-13B set cold_penalty=35% for first 15 min.
Example: base cogs_1k = 0.39 -> with cold penalty = 0.53 -> margin gap -0. (List 0.72 -> margin 0.19 vs 0.33 baseline)

Policy & ops recommendations (practical, prioritized):
1) Short-call routing (high ROI, low product risk): auto-route <=64-token requests to 7B/13B family unless customer explicitly pins model. Implement gradual rollout with an "optimize-for-cost" customer flag. (Owner: product-eng, ticket: JIRA-OPT-812)
2) Cache TTL tuning by workload: for chat-like workloads use longer prefix TTL (30m) with LRU cap; for search-like ephemeral requests use short TTL. Add per-route TTL override in Console. (Owner: infra/serving-runtime)
3) APAC reserve buffer: pre-warm minimal dedicated capacity for top 20 APAC customers that exceed 5M tokens/day to avoid cold-start multipliers during sales-driven events. (Owner: Dedicated Ops)
4) Auto-quant experiment: rollout int8 baseline for warm models, auto-fallback to int4 on low-latency bursts; track quality metrics per prompt-set. Start A/B with 5% traffic. (Owner: applied-ml)
5) Blended SKU pricing experiment: allow customers to opt into a blended per-1k price for size-aware routing; measure churn/accept rates vs cost delta. (Owner: product-marketing + finance)

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Do we have telemetry granularity to tag "short-call" vs "session-long" reliably across SDKs? Need SDK/agent work (SDK-174).
- Legal/regulatory: does routing by region across model families require reconsent for data residency-sensitive customers? (discuss with legal)
- How to quantify quality delta for int4 fallback on regression-sensitive customers (ads, codegen); likely need per-customer eval harness.

Quick action items (next 30 days):
- Build simple Canary: size-aware routing for <=64 tokens in eu-west and asia-southeast for 3 beta customers. (Owner: Marco)
- Metric dashboard: add MQL for short-call ratio, per-route cache hit, per-model ppk by region. (Owner: Lina)
- Draft blended SKU pricing note for GTM and finance (rough target: 20–35% discount vs Falcon-only for short-call bundles). (Owner: Aisha)
